title: Geometry and universal Cartier property of a line-bundle zero section
statement:
Fix the purity datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\pi:E\to B$ be a rank-one vector bundle with zero section $z:B\to E$ and underlying locally free module $\mathcal E$ [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Then $B$ and $E$ are Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact), $E$ is separated and of finite type over $k$, and $\pi$ is separated of finite type and smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There is a compactification $E\xrightarrow j\overline E\xrightarrow r B$, with $j$ an open immersion, $r$ proper and $rj=\pi$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], in which
$$\overline E=\underline{\operatorname{Proj}}_B\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_B\oplus\mathcal E),$$
and $j$ is the standard chart where the first degree-one generator is invertible [def-nagata-relative-proj].

The map $z$ is a closed immersion, $\pi z=\mathrm{id}_B$, and $D=z(B)$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Its map to $B$ is smooth of relative dimension zero and, at every $x\in D$,
$$\dim\mathcal O_{E,x}=\dim\mathcal O_{D,x}+1.$$
Here dimension is Krull dimension, the supremum of lengths of strict prime chains. The open complement $E\setminus D\hookrightarrow E$ is quasi-compact. For every scheme morphism $B'\to B$, without a flatness or Noetherian hypothesis, the base-changed zero section in $E\times_B B'$ is again an effective Cartier divisor. More precisely, on each affine frame $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset B$, the pair $(E|_U,D|_U)$ is $(\operatorname{Spec}R[t],V(t))$; on every affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R'$ over $U$ of $B'$ the pulled-back pair is $(\operatorname{Spec}R'[t],V(t))$.

proof.text: Finite type over the fixed field makes B Noetherian. Apply the existing projective-completion theorem to the canonical rank-one relative spectrum. It supplies the presentation Q, normalized dehomogenization equivalences, a proper completion with the precise chart image and equations, and separatedness, finite type and Noetherianity of the total space. Transport the compactification by V.phi: use the same ambient scheme, compose its open immersion with V.phi.hom, and retain the proper projection. The section-chart equation cancels V.phi.inv followed by V.phi.hom. The image is unchanged by precomposing with an isomorphism. Compose the projection properties with the given base morphism.

Choose the existing locally free frame cover. On each member trivializationMap_spec identifies the restricted canonical projection with affine one-space projection after an isomorphism. Affine one-space is smooth of relative dimension one; target locality gives this for the canonical projection. Transport through V.phi. The canonical zero-section specification supplies closedness and the section identity; rewriting that identity makes the zero-section composite smooth of relative dimension zero. Target locality is the IsZariskiLocalAtTarget instance for SmoothOfRelativeDimension (the chart-local definition); composition is the fixed-relative-dimension permanence theorem.

A section z of the separated smooth relative curve is a closed immersion since z followed by the projection is the identity. The canonical lift from the kernel subscheme V(ker z) to the source of z is an isomorphism (closed immersions with the same kernel). Its composite with the projection is this isomorphism, so it is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply the already-proved finite-locally-free Cartier criterion to obtain invertibility of ker z, which is exactly the effective Cartier center condition.

At a zero-section point choose an affine neighbourhood on which the invertible kernel is (t), with t a nonzerodivisor. The stalk is the flat localization of this affine ring, so the germ t′ remains a nonzerodivisor. Scheme.Hom.ker_stalkMap identifies the kernel of the closed-immersion stalk map with the extension of (t), namely (t′). Its image in the source stalk is zero, so t′ is a nonunit and belongs to the maximal ideal. The ambient stalk is Noetherian. The one-equation dimension theorem and the quotient-by-kernel isomorphism from surjectivity of the stalk map give dim O_E,z(x) = dim O_B,x + 1.
The complement is an open of the Noetherian total scheme. It has Noetherian topology, and every morphism from a Noetherian topological source is quasi-compact; apply this to the complement inclusion.

For an arbitrary B′ to B, base-change stability gives a separated smooth relative curve with projection pullback.snd. The sectionBaseChange_snd equation makes the pulled-back zero section a section of this projection. Apply the same closed-immersion and Cartier-criterion argument from Step 3. No flatness, finite type, Noetherianity or reducedness is required of B′.

For an affine frame U the first three required equations are trivializationMap_spec. Transport the pullback square defining restriction through this frame isomorphism and V.phi. Paste with the affine-space base-change square along Spec R′ to U. Its canonical pullback isomorphism identifies pullback V.p (g followed by U inclusion) with A^1_Spec R′. Compose with AffineSpace.SpecIso and the spectrum of the inverse of MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv to obtain Spec R′[t]. The coefficients equation of the polynomial equivalence identifies the projection with Spec of Polynomial.C. By the two pullback projections the base-changed section becomes the affine-space zero section: the first projection is g followed by the original zero section, using trivializationMap_spec, and the second is the identity. AffineSpace.hom_ext, on the base projection and its unique coordinate, then identifies this section with Spec of Polynomial.evalRingHom 0. Both arguments are identities of scheme morphisms over arbitrary R′.

Step 1: Sym(E) frames and R[t] by the free-module polynomial lemma (n=1); a frame change e'=ue gives t'=ut. Step 2: relative Spec is affine, so pi is qc and separated; the pointwise lft criterion and the composition lemmas 01T3/(e) give finite type and separatedness over k. Step 3: A^1 smoothness, carried over by restrict (c)/(b) and source-locality; fibre dimension 1. Step 4: P(O+E) has rank 2 and is proper by tautological geometry; the chart D+(T0) has T1'=uT1, T0'=T0, matching t'=ut, and the pieces glue to j with rj=pi. Step 5: t is a nonzerodivisor, so D is Cartier, and D->B is an isomorphism, smooth of relative dimension 0. Step 7: in R[t]_q the element t/1 is a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal, A/(t) is O_{D,x} by an explicit evaluation-kernel argument, and 00KW gives the dimension formula. Step 8: 01OW. Step 9: R[t] tensor R' = R'[t], z' is closed by 01QR, and no flatness is used. Edge cases checked: empty B, a field, k[e]/e^2, a reducible base, a nontrivial line bundle, and a non-Noetherian, non-flat B'. It is neither assumption nor a step of their proofs, and Step 4 needs it for properness: accepted. (2) affine-line-support-geometry reaches lem-poincare-compatible-primitive-roots. The only cause is that lemma's stmt_dep def-pur-affine-line-datum (Kummer and twist data), and Step 6 used the lemma just for 'B is Noetherian'.
